statement: Exactly one of these numbers is the product of three consecutive positive whole numbers. Which one?

choices.misconception: I took $1728 = 12 \times 12 \times 12$, but three equal numbers are not consecutive.
I spotted $2002 = 11 \times 13 \times 14$, but 11, 13 and 14 are not consecutive.
I checked that it is divisible by 6 and stopped, without checking that it lies between two such products.
I only checked that the number is even.

hints: What must divide any product of three consecutive numbers?
Among three consecutive numbers one is a multiple of 3 and at least one is even, so the product is a multiple of 6. Rule out choices with that, then compare with the products near the cube root.
The cube root of about 2000 is between 12 and 13. Compare with $11 \times 12 \times 13$ and $12 \times 13 \times 14$.

solutions.reliable: A product of three consecutive numbers is a multiple of 6. 2002 has digit sum 4 and 2024 has digit sum 8, so neither is a multiple of 3. That leaves 1728, 2016 and 2184. The products of three consecutive numbers near them are $11 \times 12 \times 13 = 1716$ and $12 \times 13 \times 14 = 2184$, and the next one, $13 \times 14 \times 15 = 2730$, is too big. So 2184 is the one, while 1728 and 2016 lie strictly between two such products. The transferable idea: a quick divisibility test and a bound on size eliminate most choices without any heavy calculation.

whyOnTest: Divisibility removes two choices at a glance, and bounding between neighbouring products settles the other three.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
